name: Ashvale Pressed Occasion Jacket
description:
A single-button jacket in dark navy synth-polyester blend, originally manufactured as part of a Tier 2 office uniform line and now circulating through resale markets in significant volume. The construction is utilitarian — fused interfacing rather than stitched, a single internal pocket, and shoulder seams that sit slightly wide on most frames. The lining is a slick beige acetate that catches static. Despite its origins, the jacket reads as intentionally formal from a distance, which is the point.

At Φ22, this is the most common 'occasion jacket' on the Shelf and lower Tier 2. It appears at everything from corponation subsidiary job fairs to Ouroboros insurance dispute mediations to community hall weddings. Augment-incompatible by design, though many owners have cut their own port-access slits into the back panel and hemmed the edges with iron-on tape.
cultural_context: Recognized by anyone who grew up on the Shelf as 'the hearing jacket' or 'the interview jacket' — there's only a few styles that circulate at this price point and everyone knows them. Wearing one signals you're doing your best with what you have. Some Tier 3 people feel vague discomfort when they see it; they wore the same jacket once.
story_hooks: A synthetic being attending their personhood classification hearing has been advised by their advocate to wear something that reads as 'human formal' — this jacket is what they could afford.
Two strangers at a Tier 2 job fair recognize each other's identical jackets and share a moment of wordless solidarity before the recruiter calls the first name.
A Tier 4 corponation HR rep pulls a candidate's jacket subtly to check the label during a handshake — and what she does with that information defines her character.

physical_description.visual_profile: A crisp, austere single-button blazer that reads formal despite its mass-produced origins. Dark navy creates authority; the silhouette is slightly boxy and institutional. From a distance it passes for office wear. Up close, the construction shortcuts become apparent—fused rather than sculpted, with a utilitarian precision that feels bureaucratic rather than tailored.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the shoulders with a slightly wide set; the torso is roomier than modern tailored cuts. Designed to accommodate varied body types in office environments. Sleeves hit mid-wrist. The cut accommodates augmentations poorly without modification.
physical_description.primary_material: Dark navy synth-polyester blend—durable, low-maintenance, with a subtle sheen that catches fluorescent light. Cheap interfacing fused rather than stitched into the front panels.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, almost plastic surface with minimal drape. The beige acetate lining is slick and generates static cling. Seams are tight and uniform, machine-finished. Fused panels lack natural give.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep navy blue with beige acetate lining visible at cuffs and collar roll. No pattern or accent colors—pure utilitarian monochrome.
physical_description.closures: Single button closure—dark navy resin, slightly recessed. No secondary fasteners. Buttonhole is machine-stitched and tight.
distinctive_features: Single internal patch pocket on left side
Shoulder seams sit noticeably wide, suggesting one-size-fits-most manufacturing
Fused interfacing visible as subtle ridging at lapels when examined closely
Many worn examples feature crude cut port-access slits in back panel, hemmed with iron-on tape or hand-stitching
Static-prone acetate lining catches on skin
Buttonhole tension often causes slight puckering over time
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1-2 accessible; functionally Tier 3. The gray-market resale network keeps it in constant circulation—Φ22 places it in the 'affordable formal' category where aspiration meets budget reality.
physical_description.cultural_context: Called 'the hearing jacket' or 'the interview jacket' on the Shelf—shorthand for 'doing your best with what you have.' Ubiquitous at job fairs, mediation hearings, community events, and family occasions where formality is required but budget is tight. Tier 1 corpo wearers regard it with polite distance. Tier 3 workers recognize themselves in it.
physical_description.condition_typical: New examples are pristine but cheap-feeling. Worn examples show softened sheen at collar, cuffs, and button area from handling. Static cling leaves acetate lining slightly creased. Many feature obvious back-panel alterations for augment compatibility, reducing perceived value further.
